question.text: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> stone tied at the end of a string <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> long is whirled along a vertical circle at a constant speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. What will be the tension in the string (in newton) at the bottom-most point?

solution.text:
Here, m=2 kg, r=1 m, v=4 m s-1

Tension at the bottom of the circle,

TL=mg+mv2r

=20+2×421=52 N
